newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mixed on spillover from live cattle.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mixed on spillover from live cattle.

text.p: Spillover support from the live cattle pit and expectations of bottoming action in cash hog and pork prices supported CME hog futures and prices finished mixed with nearby months higher, traders said. Pork bellies closed higher on renewed late local short covering.
Hog futures closed 0.550 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower with April up 0.350 at 73.050 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.225 to 0.875 higher with March up 0.500 at 75.250 cents.

Expectations are that the wholesale pork prices may be near a bottom as recent low prices could spark greater demand. Pork cutout values have fallen to lowest levels since early April and improvement in product values should encourage increased packer interest for cash hogs, they said.

However, hog futures could resume their fall if product values fail to improve by next week. Futures will likely trade between 71.500 and 73.500 cents per lb, basis April, until pork stabilizes, some sources estimated.

Rand Financials remained a buyer late while Lind-Waldock sold all day. R.J. O'Brien, ABN Chicogo Corp and FIMAT Futures USA also bought early while Cargill Investor Services and Refco sold earlier, traders said. In hog options, Iowa Grain was buying June 82 calls, sources said.

Pork bellies ranged mixed late before rallying at the close on local short covering. The market was influenced by action in other pits after an initial selloff linked to Wednesday's bearish weekly CME out-of-town storage report, But prices worked lower at times on expectations that Friday's Cold Storage report could also be bearish, they said.

Wednesday's out-of town report showed a larger than expected net in-movement of 1.667 million lbs last week, above the high end of estimates at 1.3 million lbs. USDA's Cold Storage report is expected to show a rise in January storings compared to a normal decline during January, they said.
"We're continuing to store bellies and big storing months of March and April are ahead," one trader said.

Analysts' expectations on Friday's report ranged from 39.7 to 43.2 million lbs in frozen storage compared with 46.5 million last year. Stocks rose during January compared with a 10-year average decline of 130,000 lbs, analysts estimated.
